title: Module scope
learningObjectives: Explain module scope and build modular, event-driven browser code.

understand.concept: Top-level declarations in an ES module are scoped to that module and do not automatically become properties of the global object. Modules are strict by default. Each module has its own lexical environment and imports/exports form explicit connections between them.
understand.whyItMatters: Module scope reduces accidental global collisions and makes dependencies explicit. Code should import the values it uses rather than relying on implicit global variables.
understand.analogy: Each module has its own workspace; only intentionally exported items are made available to other workspaces.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; module loading and DOM event behaviour follow web platform standards.

explain.narrative: internalTheme remains private to the module. defaultLanguage is exported for import by other modules.

examples.explanation: internalTheme remains private to the module. defaultLanguage is exported for import by other modules.
examples.expectedOutput: Browser console output demonstrates module or event behaviour; DOM examples require matching elements.

practise.guidedTask: Create two modules with same-named local variables. Show that they do not collide and export only the values needed elsewhere.
practise.independentTask: Build a small feature using explicit module boundaries or DOM event handling. Test keyboard, pointer, dynamic content, and failure cases as appropriate.
hints: Keep module responsibilities and public exports clear.
Preserve native keyboard and form behaviour.

questions.prompt: Do top-level module variables automatically become properties of window?
questions.explanation: Top-level declarations in modules are module-scoped rather than global-object properties.

questions.prompt: What is a good principle for modular event-driven code?
options: Use clear contracts and preserve expected browser behaviour
Stop all propagation for every event
Expose every internal module binding globally
questions.answer: Use clear contracts and preserve expected browser behaviour
questions.explanation: Explicit interfaces and predictable event handling reduce coupling and preserve usability.
